business_scope: Onion cultivation and farm-level business analysis in India. This knowledge pack covers crop, production, storage, market, cost/revenue and risk factors. Local recommendations should be adapted to season, state, variety, soil, irrigation and current market conditions.

crop_business_factors.details: Onion is cultivated mainly in kharif, late kharif and rabi seasons. Rabi production is the largest seasonal component and its harvest period creates a major storage and market-timing requirement.

Variety choice should match season, region, market requirement and storage objective. ICAR examples include Bhima Super for kharif/late kharif and Bhima Shakti for late kharif/rabi, with different maturity, yield and storage characteristics.
ICAR recommends deep, friable, well-drained soils with adequate moisture-holding capacity and organic matter; a pH around 6.0–7.5 is suitable for onion cultivation.
Production economics depend on seed quality, nursery management, fertilizer and nutrient management, irrigation, weed control and timely field operations.
Thrips, maggots and fungal diseases can reduce yield and quality. ICAR-DOGR recommends regular field scouting and integrated pest and disease management.

Onions intended for storage need proper curing/drying, careful handling, suitable ventilation and removal of damaged or rotten bulbs. Storage conditions strongly influence sprouting, rooting, rotting and weight loss.

common_risks.details: Rainfall events and adverse weather have historically caused crop damage, storage problems, supply shortages and onion price spikes.
Onion prices can change sharply because production is seasonal and supply can move quickly between surplus and shortage conditions.
Onion is semi-perishable. ICAR has reported substantial storage losses under poor storage conditions, while improved storage structures can reduce physiological weight loss, sprouting and rotting.
Thrips, maggots and fungal diseases can cause substantial yield or quality losses when not monitored and managed.
Regional concentration of production, storage and procurement can make supply more vulnerable to localized weather shocks and can affect market availability.
Holding onions for later sale requires capital to finance inventory, storage and handling while the future selling price remains uncertain.
common_risks.source: Business-analysis inference based on Government of India cost, storage and price-volatility sources

market_factors.details: The timing of kharif, late kharif and rabi arrivals influences market availability and price conditions.
Current mandi arrivals, farm-harvest prices and local market prices are critical for deciding when and where to sell.
market_factors.source: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare – ES&E

market_factors.details: For suitable rabi onions, storage can shift sales into later periods, but the decision must compare expected future price gains against storage loss, storage cost, finance cost and quality risk.
market_factors.source: ICAR; Government of India Economic Survey; business-analysis inference

market_factors.details: The Government has used procurement and buffer-stock operations and other measures to manage onion supply and price volatility.
market_factors.source: Government of India Economic Survey / consumer affairs sources

market_factors.details: Bulb quality, size, damage, curing, cleanliness, packing and storage condition influence marketability and handling losses.

Maharashtra is one of India's major onion-producing states, along with Karnataka, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar and others; regional production conditions can therefore materially affect national supply.

cost_factors: Labour for land preparation, sowing/transplanting, weeding and harvesting
Interest or working-capital cost when crop is held before sale
revenue_factors: Marketable yield per hectare or acre
Share of crop sold immediately versus stored
cost_revenue_factors.important_rule: Profitability should be calculated from the entrepreneur's actual local costs, expected marketable yield, realised price and post-harvest losses. Government cost studies provide reference data, but current local economics should be used for an individual decision.
cost_revenue_factors.source: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare – Cost of Cultivation studies

swot_factors.note: This SWOT is a synthesis of Government of India and ICAR evidence for onion cultivation in India. It is not a government-published universal SWOT for every onion farmer.
strengths: Onion is widely consumed in India throughout the year.
India has established onion-producing regions and a developed domestic market.
Different seasons and varieties provide opportunities to target different market windows.
Improved varieties and storage technologies can improve yield, quality and market timing.
weaknesses: Strong seasonality creates large changes in supply and prices.
The crop is vulnerable to post-harvest losses without suitable curing and storage.
Production is labour- and input-intensive in important cost components.
Farmer profitability can vary substantially with yield and realised market price.
opportunities: Improved varieties, seed quality and crop management can raise productivity and quality.
Improved storage can reduce losses and allow better timing of sales.
Digital/organised market information can improve selling decisions.
Government programmes and infrastructure support can improve storage and market infrastructure.
threats: Weather shocks can reduce production and disrupt storage.
Large price swings can create periods of very low or very high farmer realisations.
Pests and diseases can reduce yield and quality.
Supply gluts at major harvest periods can put downward pressure on prices.

things_to_monitor: Local and nearby market price differences
Crop stage and expected harvest date
Weather and rainfall around harvest and storage
Pest and disease incidence, especially thrips and fungal diseases
Input prices and total cost per acre/hectare
Curing and drying quality before storage
Storage loss, sprouting, rotting and weight loss
Expected price versus cost of holding the crop
Relevant government procurement, buffer-stock and market-support measures
